manuscript_claim: Adolescence is a period of pronounced neural and behavioural plasticity, and social experience during this window has a lasting influence on how an animal responds to later challenge
selected_reference: McCormick CM, Hodges TE, Simone JJ. Peer pressures: social instability stress in adolescence and social deficits in adulthood in a rodent model. Dev Cogn Neurosci 11:2-11
reference_type: review of the authors' own rodent model
why_it_supports_claim: Reviews the adolescent social-instability paradigm this study adapts, and its central argument is that peer relationships in adolescence are qualitatively distinct and that social experience at this stage is a determinant of adult social function, with long-lasting behavioural consequences. Directly supports both halves of the claim: adolescent specificity and lasting influence.
species_match_note: RAT. The manuscript sentence says 'an animal', not 'mice', so the rodent evidence is adequate; the claim is not species-specific as written. Do not use this reference to support a mouse-specific statement.
verification_source: PubMed record retrieved and abstract read in full

manuscript_claim: Among animals given the same adverse social experience, some later resemble unexposed controls on measures of affective, cognitive and physiological state while others diverge markedly from them
selected_reference: Krishnan V, Han M-H, Graham DL, et al. Molecular adaptations underlying susceptibility and resistance to social defeat in brain reward regions. Cell 131(2):391-404
why_it_supports_claim: The canonical demonstration that an INBRED mouse population given identical social defeat separates into susceptible and unsusceptible subpopulations differing across several behavioural and physiological domains. Inbreeding is what makes it load-bearing here: the divergence cannot be attributed to genetic background, which is exactly the heterogeneity the manuscript sentence describes.
verification_source: PubMed record retrieved and abstract read in full

manuscript_claim: Standard assays are administered at defined time points, are brief relative to the paradigm they assess, and are themselves mildly stressful encounters that interrupt the ongoing experience they are meant to characterise
selected_reference: Kahnau P, Mieske P, Wilzopolski J, et al. A systematic review of the development and application of home cage monitoring in laboratory mice and rats. BMC Biol 21(1):256; AND Bains RS, Wells S, Sillito RR, et al. Assessing mouse behaviour throughout the light/dark cycle using automated in-cage analysis tools. J Neurosci Methods 300:37-47
why_it_supports_claim: Kahnau states the premise directly: rodents are traditionally examined in test apparatuses OUTSIDE the home cage at selected time points, outcomes are influenced by various factors, and information is missed when animals are monitored only briefly. Bains supplies the primary mouse evidence for the comparison, concluding that home-cage monitoring across light/dark cycles yields a deeper phenotype than conventional out-of-cage phenotyping.
species_match_note: Bains is mouse; Kahnau covers mice and rats. Adequate for a claim about laboratory rodent testing practice.
verification_source: PubMed records retrieved and abstracts read in full

manuscript_claim: Radio-frequency identification tracking in the home cage makes this practical across many animals at once and over the full duration of a paradigm
selected_reference: Kahnau P, Mieske P, Wilzopolski J, et al. A systematic review of the development and application of home cage monitoring in laboratory mice and rats. BMC Biol 21(1):256
why_it_supports_claim: A systematic review of 521 publications on home-cage monitoring covering the development of automatic techniques, group-housed animals and extended recording durations. Supports the feasibility claim - that continuous, longitudinal, non-invasive monitoring of group-housed rodents is an established approach - rather than any specific result.
species_match_note: Covers mice and rats. The manuscript's own RFID implementation is described in Methods and is not supported by this citation.
verification_source: PubMed record retrieved and abstract read in full

manuscript_claim: The hippocampus is not a homogeneous structure: its subregions differ in afferent and efferent connectivity, in local circuit composition, and in the laminar organisation of inputs onto principal cells, and its non-neuronal populations are distributed unevenly across those compartments
selected_reference: Shah S, Lubeck E, Zhou W, Cai L. In situ transcription profiling of single cells reveals spatial organization of cells in the mouse hippocampus. Neuron 92(2):342-357; AND Leonardo ED, Richardson-Jones JW, Sibille E, Kottman A, Hen R. Molecular heterogeneity along the dorsal-ventral axis of the murine hippocampal CA1 field. Neuroscience 137(1):177-186
why_it_supports_claim: Shah resolves transcriptionally distinct subregions and layers within the mouse hippocampus, including distinct dentate layers and heterogeneous composition within CA1 and CA3, establishing that the structure is not molecularly uniform at subregional or laminar scale. Leonardo shows molecular heterogeneity WITHIN traditionally recognised cytoarchitectural boundaries of CA1, which is the stronger form of the claim.
verification_source: PubMed records retrieved and abstracts read in full

manuscript_claim: Stress-associated molecular adaptation need not be uniform across such a structure, and a measurement that averages across it can obscure differences that are confined to, or that differ between, particular anatomical contexts
selected_reference: Shah S, Lubeck E, Zhou W, Cai L. In situ transcription profiling of single cells reveals spatial organization of cells in the mouse hippocampus. Neuron 92(2):342-357
why_it_supports_claim: Demonstrates structure recoverable only with spatial resolution - distinct dentate layers, differing CA1 and CA3 composition, and a dorsal CA1 that is homogeneous where ventral CA1 is heterogeneous - which is precisely the structure a spatially averaged measurement would lose. Supports the measurement argument the sentence makes.
species_match_note: MOUSE. MODALITY CAVEAT: the evidence is transcriptomic and this manuscript measures protein. The sentence is written as a general measurement argument about averaging across a heterogeneous structure and does not claim proteomic precedent; it must not be reworded to imply one.
verification_source: PubMed record retrieved and abstract read in full
